encounters.cc: Severe pain in right hip after head-on motor vehicle collision where knees hit dashboard

lines: Severe pain in right hip after head-on motor vehicle collision where knees hit dashboard
He is brought to the emergency department after being involved in a head-on motor vehicle collision.
He was the restrained driver, and he reports that his knees hit the dashboard at the time of impact.
He complains of severe pain in his right hip and is unable to move his right leg.
- Open reduction internal fixation of left radial fracture, age 16
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 2 puffs (90 mcg) PRN
- Paternal grandfather: Coronary artery disease (onset age 54)
- No known history of bleeding disorders or early osteoporosis
Smoking: Current smoker, 0.5 pack per day for 4 years.
Alcohol: Heavy episodic use; intoxicated at time of accident per report.
On examination, the right leg appears shortened and internally rotated.
The patient is unable to dorsiflex his right foot.
A pelvic X-ray is performed, which shows posterior dislocation of the right hip.

encounters.cc: Neck pain and forehead laceration after high-speed motor vehicle collision while unrestrained and intoxicated

lines: Neck pain and forehead laceration after high-speed motor vehicle collision while unrestrained and intoxicated

The patient is a 23-year-old male with a history of Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, combined type, Tobacco use disorder, moderate, Alcohol use disorder, mild, and Seasonal allergic rhinitis, who presents to the Emergency Department following a motor vehicle collision approximately eighteen months after a prior collision resulting in right hip trauma.
He was the unrestrained driver, and the airbags deployed.
On arrival, he is alert but appears agitated and smells of alcohol.
His Glasgow Coma Scale score is 14 (E3V5M6).
He complains of neck pain and has a visible laceration on his forehead.
He denies any loss of consciousness and has no memory of the events leading up to the accident.
The patient is unable to provide a reliable history due to his agitation and suspected intoxication.
- Open reduction internal fixation of left radial fracture, age 16
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 2 puffs (90 mcg) PRN
- Paternal grandfather: Coronary artery disease (onset age 54)
- No known history of bleeding disorders or early osteoporosis
Smoking: Current smoker, 0.5 pack per day for 4 years.
Alcohol: Heavy episodic use; intoxicated at time of accident per report.
His vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 130/85 mmHg, heart rate 98 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air.
Physical examination reveals tenderness over the cervical spine, but no step-offs or crepitus.
Neurological examination is unremarkable with no focal deficits.

encounters.cc: Severe suprapubic pain and gross hematuria following high-speed motor vehicle collision

lines: Severe suprapubic pain and gross hematuria following high-speed motor vehicle collision
This 24-year-old male with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, combined type, and substance use disorders has presented twice previously for injuries sustained in motor vehicle collisions.
He presents to the emergency department following a high-speed motor vehicle collision.
- Open reduction internal fixation of left radial fracture, age 16
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 2 puffs (90 mcg) PRN
- Paternal grandfather: Coronary artery disease (onset age 54)
- No known history of bleeding disorders or early osteoporosis
Smoking: Current smoker, 0.5 pack per day for 4 years.
Alcohol: Heavy episodic use; intoxicated at time of accident per report.
On examination, he is hemodynamically stable but appears to be in distress due to pain.
His abdomen is soft with tenderness noted in the suprapubic region.
There is no rebound tenderness or guarding.
A pelvic X-ray reveals a right-sided pubic rami fracture.
A Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) exam is negative for free fluid in the abdomen.
A Foley catheter is placed, and gross hematuria is observed.

encounters.cc: Unconscious with significant head trauma after high-speed motor vehicle accident, intubated for airway protection

lines: Unconscious with significant head trauma after high-speed motor vehicle accident, intubated for airway protection

He is a 25-year-old male with ADHD, alcohol use disorder, and prior avascular necrosis, cervical fracture, and bladder rupture from collisions who was unrestrained and suffered significant head trauma when his car collided with a tree.
On arrival, he is unconscious and intubated for airway protection.
Over the next 48 hours, he remains in a persistent coma despite normalization of vitals and no new findings on repeat imaging.
- Open reduction internal fixation of left radial fracture, age 16
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 2 puffs (90 mcg) PRN
- Paternal grandfather: Coronary artery disease (onset age 54)
- No known history of bleeding disorders or early osteoporosis
Smoking: Current smoker, 0.5 pack per day for 4 years.
Alcohol: Heavy episodic use; intoxicated at time of accident per report.
His pupils are equal and reactive, and he demonstrates no purposeful movement in response to pain.
Head CT without contrast is obtained and is shown below.
There is no skull fracture and no large focal hematoma, but small punctate hemorrhages are visible at the gray-white matter junction and in deep brain structures.

encounters.cc: Acute dyspnea and confusion on second day of hospitalization for closed displaced right femur fracture

lines: Acute dyspnea and confusion on second day of hospitalization for closed displaced right femur fracture

The patient is a 26-year-old male with ADHD, tobacco and alcohol use disorders, and recurrent annual motor vehicle collisions resulting in avascular necrosis, cervical fracture, bladder rupture, and diffuse axonal injury, who was brought to the emergency department following another high-speed motor vehicle collision with a closed displaced right femur fracture.
After initial stabilization of the fracture, fluid resuscitation, and analgesia, he becomes acutely dyspneic and confused on the second day of hospitalization.
- Open reduction internal fixation of left radial fracture, age 16
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 2 puffs (90 mcg) PRN
- Paternal grandfather: Coronary artery disease (onset age 54)
- No known history of bleeding disorders or early osteoporosis
Smoking: Current smoker, 0.5 pack per day for 4 years.
Alcohol: Heavy episodic use; intoxicated at time of accident per report.
His oxygen saturation drops to 88% on room air.
On examination, he is tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute, heart rate is 110 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg.
Auscultation of the chest reveals bilateral crackles.
Neurological examination shows intermittent disorientation to time and place, but no focal deficits.
A petechial rash is noted around the neck and anterior chest wall.
Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows:
Chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral diffuse infiltrates.

encounters.cc: Acute dyspneic and confused 36 hours post-injury while awaiting orthopedic surgery for closed right femur fracture

lines: Acute dyspneic and confused 36 hours post-injury while awaiting orthopedic surgery for closed right femur fracture
The patient presents with orthopedic trauma following recurrent motor vehicle collisions since 2020.
He sustained a closed right femur fracture and is currently awaiting orthopedic surgery.
Approximately 36 hours post-injury, he becomes acutely dyspneic and confused.
- Open reduction internal fixation of left radial fracture, age 16
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 2 puffs (90 mcg) PRN
- Paternal grandfather: Coronary artery disease (onset age 54)
- No known history of bleeding disorders or early osteoporosis
Smoking: Current smoker, 0.5 pack per day for 4 years.
Alcohol: Heavy episodic use; intoxicated at time of accident per report.
His oxygen saturation drops to 88% on room air.
Physical examination reveals tachypnea, tachycardia, and petechial rash over his chest and axillae.
Neurological examination shows mild disorientation to time and place with no focal deficits.
Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows:
Chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral diffuse pulmonary infiltrates.
